notes:
# Aerchain visual language

The current brand is the Framer guideline at individual-core-687035.framer.app/home-ets. Ignore older purple material (#4A3ACA, Parkinsans, gradients): it is the previous brand.

## The principle

Light reveals structure. Intelligence surfaces only the part that matters. The system begins with complexity, separates what matters from noise, and marks the point where intelligence acts.

### 01 The Prism Principle

"Nothing hidden. Everything buried." Procurement data is not invisible: risks, approvals, clauses, spend patterns and supplier information already exist across fragmented systems. The problem is scale. Show complexity going in, and one clear outcome coming out ("Complexity in. Outcome owned.").

### 02 Light behaviours

How intelligence becomes visible. Something important has been surfaced, clarified or moved forward.

- **Edge Light**: a narrow edge catching directional light (architectural edges, card edges, dividers, structural surfaces).
- **Cast Shadow**: the physical consequence of directional light; it establishes materiality, depth, structure, rhythm and proof that the light source is real.
- **Beam Light**: a directional plane or ray travelling from a clear source.
- **Refraction**: a beam separating at a defined point. It stays grey and orange, directional, structural and simple.
- **Point Light**: a single localised mark of illumination, for an anomaly, a signal point, a resolved state, a decision moment or a data marker.

Draw light as one clean shape (a beam, a V, a funnel) with one tone inside. Stepped heights read as a bar chart; avoid them.

### 03 Signal Fields

Intelligence moving through complexity. Every line represents something real: a supplier, bid, PO, contract, invoice, workflow or data signal. The point of action is where one moment resolves them: "Every rate, risk, and approval, scattered, until one moment resolves them."

### 04 Iconography

One system, two constructions. Plain icons use an outline construction. AI-touched icons use the parallel-line construction: orange identifies the portion where intelligence has acted, grey represents the underlying system or manual baseline. They do not share the same grid. Both have light and dark versions.

### Material ground

Procurement is physical. Material is not decoration: it represents the physical world behind procurement (materials, surfaces, infrastructure, objects).

### Photography

Photography makes the visual philosophy physical and believable, with the same idea of light surfacing something important.

## The Field

One construction grid; four things light does to it. Parallel lines are the foundation: every graphic device is built from this grid.

- **The 2:1 stroke ratio**: the gap is always exactly half the stroke weight. Scale them together, never change the proportion. In films at 1080p: 8 px strokes, 4 px gaps, a 12 px pitch.
- **Three roles**: the construction stays the same; what changes is how loud the field is and whether it carries orange at all. At background role the field is texture and may modulate freely without a light source. Supporting and hero roles carry structure, and only the hero role carries orange, at the point of action.
- **Layout**: copy sits on grey, never on orange. The field can run the full frame with text over it; copy must not touch the lit portion.
- **Lines**: each line is one continuous flat stroke in one colour; lines flow in one direction and never bend back or drop to the floor. Each colour is a flat field with slightly darker gaps (black #1E1E1E with #141414 gaps, orange #F55A00 with #DB5000, stone #D3CCBF with #C2BAAC). Black gaps through orange or stone read as loud barcode stripes: don't.

## Colour

Three controlled single-hue ramps of 16 steps, light to dark:

- **Signal** (orange), primary Signal 9 #F55A00. Signal fill is the resolved action: once per screen.
- **Stone** (warm neutral), primary Stone 9 #837E73. Grounds and most surfaces.
- **Steel** (blue grey), primary Steel 850 #7E858B. Systems, data, secondary structure.

Films use the tuned values from the Aerchain speaker post (the "Film fields" ramp): stone ground #E9E5DD, ink #141414, muted copy #6B665E, black field #1E1E1E, orange #F55A00. Keep them: they are what the shipped films are drawn with.

Flat colour only. Nothing glows, blurs or uses shadows.

## Shape

The cut corner is the shadow. A chamfer on the bottom-right corner only; the cut equals a quarter of the element's height, rounded to the nearest pixel. A second chamfer contradicts the light direction. Pressed buttons close the chamfer and go flat. One Signal (orange) filled button per screen; everything else is Stone. The Agent button carries the Intelligence Square and is the only outlined button allowed to be orange.

## Type

Bricolage Grotesque everywhere in Aerchain artwork (headlines SemiBold 600 with the opsz axis at display size, tracking -1%; body Regular 400). It is the face the guideline itself is set in. Interface chrome of tools is not artwork.

## Logo

The AERCHAIN wordmark: letters in black (light grounds) or light stone (dark grounds), the "ai" mark always orange #F55A00. Never recolour the ai mark, never add effects, give it clear space of at least its letter height. The ai mark alone may stand in as a small signature. In copy, write Aerchain.

## Motion

- Colour arrives from the right, line by line, the bottom line first (a rising staircase), and leaves the way it came.
- Moves set off gently and settle (the landing ease); no bounce, no overshoot.
- Orange lands last and once: the point of action.
- Black returns from the middle outwards to close a loop.
- The cover frame (the "Cover" mark) shows the resolved idea.

## Sound

Clean, minimal, digital: soft ticks, filtered noise whooshes as colour arrives from the right, a low pulse underneath, one bright accent when orange lands. Never cheesy or busy. Leave room for speech and duck under dialogue. About -16 LUFS for social.

## Words

Write Aerchain (never AERCHAIN in copy) and SpendOS. Plain, confident sentences about outcomes. No em dashes.


## More from the guideline

### Iconography in detail
- **Outline icons**: a 14 x 14 grid, 1 unit stroke, corners chamfered at 40 degrees. For ordinary actions and objects.
- **AI-touched icons**: built from parallel lines in the 2:1 ratio. Orange marks only the part where intelligence acted; grey is the system underneath.

### Signature frames
- **Human Checkpoint**: lines run through two chamfered brackets that hold an orange outline person: the moment a human approves or decides.
- **Complexity in. Outcome owned.**: the poster line for Signal Fields, many lines in, one lit outcome.
- **Point of Action**: the layout where one orange element resolves a busy field.

### Marks
- The AERCHAIN wordmark is the default signature.
- The lockup adds the line "AI-NATIVE SPEND OS" under the wordmark, between short orange rules (logos/lockup-spend-os.svg, for light grounds).
- A white wordmark (logos/wordmark-white.svg) is for dark grounds.
- Some posters use a triangle A mark with a lowercase "Aerchain".

### Pattern generator
The guideline's own pattern tool builds line fields in seven modes (Falloff, Steps, Resolve, Prism, Signal, Comb, Wave) and four arrangements (Single, Dual, Triple, Mirror). Use these names when asking for a field.

### Type in practice
The guideline is set in Bricolage Grotesque; Inter appears only inside interface widgets. A print example (an A4 cover, sizes in points): eyebrow 10 / 500 / tracking +0.1, title 50 / SemiBold 600 / leading 1.0 / tracking -0.5, subtitle 13 / 400 / leading 1.4, tagline 11.5 / 500, footer 7.5 / 400 / tracking +0.1.

### Into Figma
SVG text only imports as editable text when the font family is the PostScript name (BricolageGrotesque-SemiBold). A weight alone maps 600 to Bold, and letter spacing is dropped.
